# **CFTC and ETF Report** _A weekly update of futures and exchange traded fund activity._ - In price terms, gold and silver underperformed in the first half of February. Both metals struggled with a touch of Dollar strength. Gold lost ground but still remains comfortably above $1,720 with investors positioned for the next upwards move. Silver investors are bullish too but the price traded sideways during this period. The platinum group metals performed much more impressively. Palladium forced its way through $700 and has since found robust support whenever it has fallen below this level. Platinum was the star performer, closing the gap on gold as supply disruptions in South Africa reminded the market that perhaps fundamentals might have some relevance after all. - Each of gold, silver, platinum and palladium experienced increases in net speculative futures and options positioning. To a large extent, these “flows” seem to be a return to a more normal level of risk exposure than was seen during the large risk-off move seen in the last few months of last year. • All of the major precious metals recorded net inflows into their ETFs. Gold flows were thin, suggesting unconvincing market sentiment. Silver and platinum saw reasonable buying interest but palladium was the major winner as US investors returned in numbers. After seeing some buying interest in the previous week, there were no changes in rhodium ETF holdings. ##### **David Jollie** **david.jollie@mitprecious.com Tel: +44 20 7489 6767** **13 February 2012** ##### **New York:** 200 Park Avenue, New York, NY 10166 0130 Tel: +1 212 878 4122 ##### **London:** 4th Floor, St Martins Court, 10 Paternoster Row, London EC4M 7BB Tel: +44 20 7489 6767 ##### **Hong Kong:** Suite 1306, Two Exchange Square, 8 Connaught Place, Central, Hong Kong Tel: +852 2899 2026 ##### **Tokyo:** 2-1 Ohtemachi 1-Chome, Chiyoda-Ku, Tokyo 100 Tel: +81 33 285 3407 ##### **Singapore:** 80 Robinson Road, #15-02, Singapore, 068898 Tel: +65 6372 8050 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **13 February 2012** ### **Gold CFTC data to 7 February 2012; ETF data to 10 February 2012.** #### **Exchange (COMEX and TOCOM) and ETF Gold Investment (oz)** ||**COMEX**

E)**|**ZKB**|**ETFS (US +UK)**|**Julius Baer**|**Xetra**|**Total**| |**03-Feb-12**|41,061,167|5,712,459|3,833,426|393,901|1,298,050|7,222,540|5,612,067|3,458,912|1,639,139|**70,231,661**| |**10-Feb-12**|41,109,761|5,763,635|3,814,429|393,901|1,297,951|7,234,248|5,627,792|3,458,262|1,639,139|**70,339,118**| |**Change**|**48,594**|**51,176**|**-18,997**|**0**|**-99**|**11,708**|**15,725**|**-650**|**0**|**107,457**| - Having gained strongly during January, the gold price has weakened a little in the first part of February. The Dollar stopped falling and has firmed a little, placing the precious metal complex under some pressure. At the start of the month, gold was climbing following the FOMC’s comments on their expectations of maintaining interest rates at a low level for an extended period. Gold climbed to $1,760 on the 3rd of February before positive US non-farm payroll data drove the price back down to $1,720 at the start of the following week. This positive news enabled the Dollar to show some strength finally and the increasingly labyrinthine discussions over Greek debt helped soften the Euro too. The Dollar weakened sharply on the 7th on an outbreak of short-lived optimism that the Greek talks might conclude successfully that day and gold leapt to $1,750. As confidence in the likelihood of any deal slowly evaporated, the Dollar firmed again and gold fell back towards $1,730. Looking forwards, this relationship to risk makes price moves hard to call: even the apparent resolution of the current phase of the Greek crisis appears to have had no positive or negative effect on the price. We do, however, believe the current consolidation phase is more likely to end with a move upwards than a move downwards. - Net long speculative positions on COMEX climbed by a further 1.25 million ounces in the week to the 7th of February, rising to 24.1 million ounces, despite a slight decline in the gold price. Long contracts held in both non-commercial and non-reportable positions increased, suggesting that the market is looking for another move upwards in price once the current consolidation is over. - A net 107,000 ounces of gold was purchased by ETF investors in the week to the 10th of February. Of the major funds which we monitor, four recorded net inflows but the Lyxor fund recorded net outflows. The low total flows and the mixture of buying and selling fit in with the directionless nature of moves in the gold price in recent days as investors look for concrete signs for progress, or a lack of progress over Greek debt talks. #### **Gold Exchange Investment, Jan 10 — Feb 12** 40 2,000 Gold price, $/oz

||||||| |**Date**|**iShares**|**ZKB**|**ETFS (UK)**|**ETFS (US)**|**Julius Baer**|**Total**|| |**03-Feb-12**|310,227,234|80,017,410|28,545,165|21,540,320|15,605,983|**455,936,112**|| |**10-Feb-12**|311,879,302|82,035,561|28,379,230|21,540,320|15,605,983|**459,440,396**|| |**Change**|**1,652,068**|**2,018,151**|**-165,935**|**0**|**0**|**3,504,284**|| - After a remarkably rapid rise in January, the first half of February was essentially neutral for silver, which traded almost exclusively between $33.20 and $34.40. The gold:silver ratio changed little and, unsurprisingly, moves in the silver price echoed those in the gold price. Where the Dollar had weakened for much of January, it started to strengthen in early February on relatively positive US data and the usual concerns over Greek and other European debt. As with gold, there were sharp, currency-driven movements on the 3rd (lower following the release of US payroll data) and on the 7th (upwards, driven by unexpected optimism over Greece). It is currently trading close to $33.80 following the announcement of some agreement over Greece and Europe’s apparent entry into a Brave New World. We continue to worry about silver demand and about the challenges ahead for Greece in implementing yet another round of austerity. - For the sixth week in a row, silver investors ignored the metal’s underlying fundamentals and added to their long exposure. Net long speculative positions soared by 33.1 million ounces to 194.3 million ounces. This is their highest level since silver slipped below $40 in September last year. News late last week of margin reductions in silver on COMEX could help drive additional buying interest this week, particularly if the gold price appreciates. - Silver ETF positions grew by 3.5 million ounces in the week to th

e 10th of February having grown by 3.8 million ounces in the previous week. Swiss and North American investors were both weighty buyers. Total metal holdings are now approaching the 460 million ounce mark and a third successive week of net buying could indicate a turnaround to more positive sentiment by these investors. #### **Silver Exchange Investment, Jan 10 — Feb 12** 375 50 Silver price, $/oz

||||||| |**Date**|**ZKB**|**ETFS (UK)**|**ETFS (US)**|**Julius Baer**|**Other**|**Total**|| |**03-Feb-12**|368,856|384,550|480,559|106,640|106,971|**1,447,576**|| |**10-Feb-12**|366,975|380,711|495,397|108,640|106,971|**1,458,694**|| |**Change**|**-1,881**|**-3,839**|**14,838**|**2,000**|**0**|**11,118**|| - Platinum was the start performer in price terms during the first two weeks of February. While gold slid lower, platinum accelerated, rising from a short-lived low of $1,580 at the end of January to its current $1,662. During this period, the goldplatinum spread moved in platinum’s favour, sliding from almost $150 at the start of the month to just over $60 currently. The key driver seemed to be a number of supply side issues in the South African mining industry, most importantly the illegal strike at the Impala Lease Area which broke out in January. As the significance of this strike became increasingly apparent, platinum outperformed gold, rising to $1,635 on the 3rd of February and only dropping to $1,610 on the 6th when the Dollar firmed. The jump higher on the 7th (driven by

possible progress on the Greek talks) saw platinum leap to $1,670 on the 9th. Given that Impala has now started rehiring and expects to restart production in the next few weeks, it will be interesting to see if platinum can continue to close in on the gold price. - Platinum net long speculative positions increased by only 24,000 ounces on NYMEX and 9,000 ounces on TOCOM in the first week of February, rising to a combined 1.61 million ounces, mainly due to short covering, a third higher than at the start of the year. - There were net inflows of platinum into the ETFs (11,100 ounces) for the sixth successive week, taking total holdings up to 1.46 million ounces. Although buying over this period has not been frantic, it has amounted to 57,000 ounces. If annualised, this would be in excess of 500,000 ounces, a figure that should make the market take note when combined with supply side constraints in South Africa. #### **Platinum Exchange Investment Jan 10 — Feb 12** 2,500 2,000

||||||| |**Date**|**ZKB**|**ETFS (UK)**|**ETFS (US)**|**Julius Baer**|**Other**|**Total**|| |**03-Feb-12**|402,386|470,363|665,690|123,243|164,189|**1,825,871**|| |**10-Feb-12**|387,256|474,098|710,036|123,243|169,888|**1,864,521**|| |**Change**|**-15,130**|**3,735**|**44,346**|**0**|**5,699**|**38,650**|| - Although it was less impressive than platinum, the palladium price firmed during the first half of February. The bare figures show it rising from $685 to a high of $717 on the

9th before slipping back to the current levels of a few Dollars over $700. The key question seemed to be the support and resistance to be found at this psychologically-important level. ETF buying of metal was substantial, demonstrating the significance of round numbers in some investors’ thinking. Palladium eventually climbed through the $700 barrier on the 2nd of February and then broke through its 200 day moving average in reaching a high of $1715 on the 3rd. The price dipped below $700 on the 6th and 7th but bounced back quickly enough to show some resilience. A move higher to $717 on the 9th failed to break the bears’ resolve and palladium fell back again. It dipped below $700 again on the 10th but is currently trading just above this troublesome level. - Futures investors opened new positions in palladium and covered shorts too in the first week of February once the price had climbed over $700 an ounce. Net long NYMEX positions climbed by 247,000 ounces to 1.2 million ounces. This was the largest weekly increase since June 2011 and the highest long positioning since September 2011. The $700 level seems increasingly important in terms of maintaining investor interest in this metal. - Palladium was the major winner amongst the precious metals in ETF terms. Investors purchased a net 38,650 ounces. Sentiment has firmly switched from selling to buying amongst ETF investors. US investors bought 44,000 ounces, their highest weekly purchase since December 2010. So far this year, global investors have bought a net 128,000 ounces, driving holdings up to 1.86 million ounces. #### **Palladium Exchange Investment, Jan 10 — Feb 12** 2,000 1,000
